question.problem:
The projection of the intersection between the hyperbolic paraboloid $12z=4(x+2)^{2}-3{y}^{2}$ and the plane 
$z=1$  onto the $xy$-plane is a hyperbola. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the hyperbola?
question.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the paraboloid and the plane $z=1$, we substitute $z=1$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}12z & =4(x+2)^{2}-3{y}^{2} \\ 12(1) & =4(x+2)^{2}-3{y}^{2} \\ 12 & =4(x+2)^{2}-3{y}^{2} \\ 1 & =\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} \\ 1 & =\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbola with semi-axes of lengths $\sqrt{3}$ and $2.$
